info.name: Football Data Platform API
info.description:
FotMob-backed Django REST API.

Every route is served from the local database: no request triggers an upstream FotMob fetch.

## Getting started

There is no login or registration flow in this collection. The API runs with one fixed user and one long-lived token.

1. On the server, read the token:

       manage.py create_api_token

2. Paste it into the `token` variable (it is pre-filled for the local dev user). Collection-level auth then sends `Authorization: Token {{token}}` on every request.
3. Set `base_url` (default `http://localhost:8000`). `base_url` and `token` are the only variables.
4. Run **Token check > Verify token (me)** to confirm it works.

Every other value - match, league, team, season, player and run IDs, dates and request bodies - is written literally into that request's path, query string or body, so each request is self-contained and editable where you read it. The IDs default to the sample FA Cup fixture (match `6469292`, league `953430`, team `674304`); if your database holds different data, run **Matches > List matches** and copy an ID from its results.

## Roles

The single token is minted with the `admin` role, so every endpoint in this collection is permitted, including the staff-only internal routes and the administrator-only overrides. Requests are still labelled `(staff)` or `(admin)` so the required privilege is visible if narrower tokens are issued later:

| Role | Can |
| --- | --- |
| reader | GET only |
| staff | + manual matches, allowed-field edits, soft delete, internal reads |
| admin | + overrides |

Mint a narrower one with `manage.py create_api_token --username reader --role reader`.

## Conventions

- Lists return `{count, next, previous, results}`; `page_size` defaults to 50 and is capped at 200.
- Errors return `{code, message, details, request_id}`.
- Coverage features return `{available, state, fetched_at, source_coverage_level, entry_count, data}`; `state` is one of `not_fetched`, `available`, `empty`, `unavailable`, `failed`.
- Unknown scores are `null`, never `0`.

item.name: Players
item.description:
Players are a by-product of coverage ingestion: FotMob has no player list endpoint in this integration, so a `Player` row appears the first time the player shows up in an ingested lineup, match event or player-stats block.

If these return empty or 404, run **Scrapers (run ingestion) > Coverage** first - for one match, use **Coverage - specific match IDs**. The IDs below are local primary keys, not FotMob IDs.

request.description: Every player stored so far, newest coverage first. Populated by coverage ingestion; `search` matches the name.
Local primary key. Players are created from ingested lineups, so this returns 404 until coverage has been synced.
Matches where the player appears in a stored lineup or event. Returns 404 until players exist.

item.name: Scrapers (run ingestion)
item.description:
Runs the two FotMob scrapers through the API instead of the shell. Each request posts to `/api/internal/sync-jobs/`, which hands the job to a background worker and answers **202** immediately - the fetching never happens inside the response, so Postman does not sit waiting for thousands of fixtures.

**How to use a request here**

1. Send it. You get 202 with a `status_url`, or **409** if that same job is already running.
2. Poll **Latest run for a job** (or **Runs in progress**) until `state` is no longer `running`. The run record then carries the counts, provider request and error totals and the duration.
3. On a failure, **Latest run errors** lists the categorized errors and the quarantined payloads.

**Every request here is `"dry_run": true`.** A dry run fetches from FotMob and classifies everything but writes nothing, which is the safe way to check a window first. Set `"dry_run": false` to persist.

Scope is bounded server-side: at most 60 past/future days, a 121-day explicit range, 14 days back for live and coverage, 500 matches per coverage run and 50 explicit IDs. One run of a given job at a time.

Cron does not use this route - it runs the same jobs as management commands straight against the ORM, with `flock` for locking. This endpoint is the staff-only manual equivalent, and the worker thread is a development convenience, not a production queue.

request.description:
**This is how you get player data.** One matchDetails call writes the lineups, per-player stats, squad links and event-to-player links for that match, which is what creates `Player` rows - there is no separate player scraper.

The example is LaLiga match 5868121 (xG coverage): 46 players, 46 squad links and ~900 stat rows. Swap in any completed match ID from **Matches > Completed matches**; a top-division fixture gives the richest data, while lower-coverage matches may have no lineups at all.

To populate many matches at once use **Coverage - fill gaps**, which walks recently completed matches whose coverage is missing.
